tax.flatRateNote: 25% flat capital-income tax plus 5.5% solidarity surcharge on it; no church tax.
notes: The saver's allowance (Sparerpauschbetrag) is €1,000 a year for a single person, shared across all banks and brokers via exemption orders (Freistellungsaufträge).

Accumulating funds pay a yearly advance tax (Vorabpauschale): fund value at the start of the year × 70% of the Basiszins (3.20% for 2026), capped at the fund's actual gain that year. In the year of purchase it shrinks by one twelfth for every full month before the purchase month. It is deducted in January of the following year and credited when you sell.

Private-sale rules (directly held crypto, gold ETCs with a delivery right): gains are tax-free after 12 months. Sold sooner, gains are taxed at your personal income-tax rate, but only if all private-sale gains of the year reach €1,000 (an exemption limit, not an allowance).
Losses on shares/funds can only offset gains in the same category; your broker keeps loss pots automatically.

education.title: All at once or in steps?
education.text: Vanguard compared investing a lump sum at once with spreading it over 12 months (MSCI World, 1976–2022): the lump sum came out ahead in about 68% of rolling one-year periods, because markets rose more often than they fell. Spreading the purchases mainly reduces the damage, and the regret, if prices fall soon after you buy.

source.label: Vanguard: Cost averaging — invest now or temporarily hold your cash?

education.title: What the stress test measures
education.text: Beta is how much an instrument has tended to move for each 1% move of the world index (weekly returns, last 3 years). The episode columns repeat what each instrument actually did during the real falls of the world index, scaled to your scenario. Neither is a forecast: the next fall can hit an instrument harder than any of these.
